# Alpen Zenith ZR-7 DH Configuration - Updated Research Findings

## 1. PRODUCT OVERVIEW


Alpen High Performance Products has been leading the way in climate-responsive design for over four decades, headquartered in Colorado, serving the entire U.S. with an expansive dealer network
. 
The Zenith series features long strand pultruded fiberglass frame that provides superior strength and thermal performance, with super-insulating closed-cell foam in both the frame and sash cavities
. 
The Alpen Zenith Series is divided up into 5 different product lines, including the ZR-5 or 525, ZR-6 or 626, ZR-7 or 725, ZR-9 or 925, and the ZR-10 or 1025 series
. The DH configuration indicates a double-hung window style.

## 2. CONFIRMED FINDINGS

### Performance Specifications
- **Frame Material**: 
Long strand pultruded fiberglass frame provides superior strength and thermal performance

- **Glazing Technology**: 
Triple and quad-pane ThinGlass ensures exceptional thermal efficiency and durability

- **ZR-7/725 Series Performance**: 
Offering NFRC-certified whole-window performance of up to a 0.14 U-Value (R-7.1 insulating factor), and center-of-glass U-Value performance up to 0.11 (R-9.1 insulating factor), 725 Series windows and doors can also be configured to meet both Passive House Institute U.S. (PHIUS) and International Living Building Institute/Living Building Challenge standards

- **Air Infiltration**: 
Air infiltration rates as low as 0.01 CFM per square foot offer exceptional air-tightness and energy efficiency

- **Double-Hung Sizing**: 
Double-hung (up to 55-in. by 91-in.)


### Construction Features
- **Weatherstripping**: 
Advanced sealing technology provides protection against water damage and air infiltration (as low as 0.01 CFM per square foot)

- **Spacer System**: 
High-performance spacers and inert gas fill, along with four independent low-e surfaces in the glass assembly

- **Insulation**: 
Super-insulating closed-cell foam in both the frame and sash cavities enhances thermal insulation

- **Gas Retention System**: 
Proprietary, tested "any altitude" gas retention system adjusts to all locations and altitudes


### Certifications and Standards
- **AAMA Certification**: 
Zenith windows are built to withstand severe weather conditions and hold the AAMA certification for exceptional wind, water, and air resistance

- **NFRC Certification**: 
Products proudly bear NFRC certification, ensuring top-notch quality and performance

- **Energy Star**: 
Many door and window styles have earned ENERGY STAR® Most Efficient certification

- **Passive House**: 
Alpen was the first North American window manufacturer to achieve dual certification from both PHIUS and PHI

- **DECLARE Label**: 
Zenith is the first North American window certified under the Living Building Challenge Declare label "Red List Approved"


### Warranty Information
- **Coverage**: 
The windows and doors come with a limited lifetime warranty for the original owner

- **Transferability**: 
It only applies to subsequent owners for a period of 10 years

## 5. YELLOW FINDINGS

### Mixed Customer Service Experience (2018-2023)

Customer service concerns reported by GBA users: "The only hitch has been customer service. We had some issues as delivered and unfortunately are still working through getting them resolved. IT seems we have a good team in place now, but it took 12 months of a barrage of contacts to get them to respond, then the fixes were only partial and very halting"
. However, 
users hoped this "can be chalked up to the pandemic rush and attendant labor shortage and hope it is getting better"
.

Additional service concerns: 
Salt Lake City installation had "issues with a door handle and lock and the customer service was really poor - very slow responses"
.

Contrasting positive experience: 
Customer service comparison showed "customer service let us down with all companies *except* ComfortLine Fiberframe. The customer service at ComfortLine Fiberframe was superb. The salesman we dealt with—Tom Mehrman—was sooo responsive and helpful"
.

### Quality Control Issues (2018)

One GBA user reported: "8 of the elements in the windows available for delivery had flaws, ranging from imperfections essentially not visible to the naked eye to one broken pane. Meanwhile, our contractor was poised to de-mobilize resources (aka pull of the job) because of the delay. I took delivery of the windows as is"
.

### Installation Complexity

Contractors find the breather tube/balloon system unusual: "One thing that weirds-out contractors are the little balloons. It is a bit of a pain to seal and set the capillary tubes behind the glazing strips"
, though this is a design feature for high-altitude performance, not a defect.
